Order 
The present petition has been filed by the petitioner under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. against the judgement and order dated 04.10.2023 passed in Cr.R. No.544/2023 by the Sessions Court whereby, order dated 27.08.2022 passed by the JMFC , Morena has been affirmed and revision has been dismissed on the ground of delay.

2. Brief facts of the case are that the complainant filed a private complaint against the petitioner and other co-accused persons namely-Suresh Singh and Dharmendra Singh with effect that the complainant was in want of a residential house in Morena for the residential purpose of her children and she stated that she mat the accused through the assistance of her brother Ramnaresh Tomar and his friend Rajendra Tiwari.

She further stated that accused assured her that, one plot of their ownership and possession is situated in village Jora Khurd Tehsil and Dist.- Morena which is the part of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4439 2 MCRC-54256-2023 the survey No.357 and measuring 1000 sq. feet,92.93 sq. meter at old ward No 30 and new ward No26 which show the complainant liked.
She further stated that in front of Ramnaresh Tomar and Rajendra Tiwari, the deal was fixed with the accused.
In presence of his brother, she has given the amount to Ramnaresh Gurjar.

On 09-01-2015, co-accused executed the registry in favour of the complainant and at the time of executing the registry Ramnaresh Gurjar, and Dharmendra Gurjar were present and assisted in the writing in the documents.
The aforesaid registered sale deed was executed by Shri Brijmohan Kushwah in which her brother Ramnaresh Tomar and Rajendra Tiwari had signed as witnesses.
When the complainant reached to the patwari of the concern circle.
Then the patwari informed her that, survey No 357 is a part of National Highway No 3 and there in no such plot on the spot and some one has committed fraud with complainant.

Then she approached to the S.P. Morena, I.G.
Chambal Zone but no action was taken against the accused persons.

Hence, complainant filed a Ramnaresh vs Smt. Sunita on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83102158/

sentences.text: Over the aforesaid complaint, court below after recording the evidence u/s 200 of Cr.P.C. has taken cognizance against the present petitioner and other co-accused persons.

Against the order of the trial court, the petitioner approached the revisional court and the revisional court dismissed his petition without touching the merits of the case only on the ground of delay.
Hence, this petition has been filed.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the orders passed by the courts below are contrary and against the law.
The revision of the petitioner has been dismissed without touching its merits only on the basis of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4439 3 MCRC-54256-2023 the being time barred.
The Hon'ble Apex Court has given catena of judgements that in the cases of time barred petitions, the lenient view should be adopted by the Courts.
The cognizance has been taken over the private complaints, because as no case was made out against the present petitioner, her complaint was not registered.
But, the trial court without appreciating the material available on record in proper manner, has passed and arbitrary order.
4. From perusal of the order of the trial court at Paragraph-5, it is clear that the present applicant was only allegedly present on the spot of the occurrence.

Merely, on the basis of the presence, the offences are not made out against the petitioner under Section 420, 467, 468 and 471 of the IPC,
unless and until there is clear and evident active participation of the petitioner.
5. It is further argued that neither any transaction has been made by the present petitioner or in favour of the present petitioner.
He is neither the beneficiary nor the executor of the alleged sale deed, in any manner.
No money has been received by the petitioner.
No Registry or deed has been signed by the petitioner.
Only, the present petitioner's being an advocate, he has been falsely implicated in this case.
He only drafted some relevant documents in this regard that too unknowingly.
The sale deed was executed between the respondent-Smt. Sunita and accused- Suresh.
The present petitioner is in no manner concerned with the aforesaid alleged forgery of sale of any land.

Hence, in the present facts and circumstance, where no NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:4439 4 MCRC-54256-2023 active participation is there, the order of the trial court is arbitrary and deserves to be quashed.
The order of the revisional court also suffers from technical faults while dismissing a criminal case only on the ground of being time barred.

Hence,
this petition may be allowed and the orders dated 04.10.2023 passed by the Sessions Court and order dated 27.08.2022 passed by the JMFC, Morena be quashed.
6.
Learned counsel for the respondent vehemently opposed the prayer and prayed for its rejection by supporting the impugned orders.
He further argued that the from the paragraph No.5 of the order of the trial court, itself, it is clear that the petitioner/accused received certain money in cash from the respondent.
It is further argued that the present petitioner in connivance with other co-accused persons sold a Government land allotted for national highway which in itself is a major offence.
There is enough evidence material available on record to prove that prima facie case is made out against the petitioner.
Hence, the petition being misconceived deserves to be quashed.

2 7.
Hear counsel for the rival parties and perused the entire record with due care.

8. The core legal issued before this Court are that:-
Whether cognizance under Section 420,467, 471 of IPC can be quashed at the threshold merely on the ground that the petitioner was allegedly "only present at the spot".
Whether the revisional Court acted illegally in dismissing the revision solely on the ground of delay.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4439 5 MCRC-54256-2023
Whether inherent jurisdiction under Section 482 Cr.P.C. can be invoked to bypass statutory limitation and revive a time-barred revision.

9. At the outset, it is well settled that at the stage of taking cognizance, the Magistrate is required to see whether the allegations prima facie disclose commission of an offence and not to conduct a detailed examination of the defence of the accused.
10.

The Supreme Court in Amit Kapoor v. Ramesh Chander (2012) 9 SCC 460 and Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. v. State of Maharashtra (2021) 6 SCC 657 has categorically held that the High Court, while exercising inherent jurisdiction, cannot evaluate the sufficiency of evidence or adjudicate upon disputed questions of fact.

sentences.text: 11. Whether the petitioner was merely present at the spot or had actively participated in the alleged act of cheating, and whether there existed dishonest intention from the inception, are pure questions of fact , which can be adjudicated only after evidence is led before the trial Court.
12. The allegations of receiving money in cash are there against the present applicant, which prima facies the commission of the offence by the present petitioner.

13. As regards the dismissal of the revision, it is evident that the revision was filed with an inordinate delay of nearly ten months and the petitioner failed to furnish any satisfactory explanation for such delay.

Law of limitation has to be applied with full rigour and cannot be diluted on sympathetic or equitable considerations, as held by the Supreme Court in NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4439 6 MCRC-54256-2023 P.K. Ramachandran v. State of Kerala (1997) 7 SCC 556.

sentences.text: Revisional jurisdiction being discretionary in nature, the revisional Court was fully justified in declining to entertain a stale and time-barred revision.
The inherent powers of this Court under Section 482 Cr.P.C. cannot be invoked to indirectly revive a time-barred remedy or to circumvent statutory limitation.
14. In view of the aforesaid legal position, this Court finds no illegality, perversity or jurisdictional error in the impugned orders passed by the trial Court and the revisional Court.
